title: Multiplication by any positive integer is an fppf cover of a semiabelian scheme
statement: Let $S$ be a normal integral locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], where normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $p:G\to S$ be a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with identity $e$. The addition, inverse and identity are $S$-morphisms satisfying the commutative group identities; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Assume every geometric fibre is semiabelian: after an algebraically closed residue-field extension $k$, it fits into an exact sequence of fppf sheaves $1\to\mathbf G_{m,k}^r\to G_k\to A_k\to1$, where $r\geq0$, $\mathbf G_{m,k}=\operatorname{Spec}k[t,t^{-1}]$, and $A_k$ is a proper smooth geometrically connected $k$-group scheme. For every integer $d\geq1$, the homomorphism $[d]:G\to G$, the sum of $d$ copies of the identity, is flat, surjective, quasi-finite and of finite presentation. Here flat means that its local ring maps are flat, surjective refers to underlying points, and quasi-finite means finite type with finite fibres. In particular $[d]$ is an fpqc covering (faithfully flat and quasi-compact), without any invertibility condition on $d$. For $a\geq1$ its iterated relation schemes $R_a=G\times_{[d],G,[d]}\cdots\times_{[d],G,[d]}G$ with $a$ factors are flat and of finite presentation over $S$, hence locally Noetherian. Their restriction over an open of $S$ is the corresponding relation scheme for the restricted multiplication map. No assertion that $[d]$ is finite or etale over $S$ is made.

source.place: II 3.3.2.1, proof: multiplication on a connected semistable group is surjective, flat and quasi-finite, used again for descent in II 3.3.3. Local original WANTED. The assertions about relation schemes are its base-change and composition consequences.

proof.text:
Fix $d\geq1$. Work first over an algebraically closed residue-field extension $k$, and write $H=G_k$ and $0\to T\to H\to A\to0$ for its given semiabelian presentation. For $T=\mathbf G_m^r$, the pullback of $[d]_T$ by a point $(u_1,\ldots,u_r)$ over $\operatorname{Spec}C$ is
$$\operatorname{Spec} C[z_1,\ldots,z_r]/(z_1^d-u_1,\ldots,z_r^d-u_r).$$
Each $z_i$ is automatically a unit, with inverse $u_i^{-1}z_i^{d-1}$. Successively applying [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free] gives a free $C$-basis $\prod_i z_i^{a_i}$, $0\leq a_i<d$, of size $d^r$. This algebra has the displayed finite presentation; its module is flat by [lem-sc-affine-standard-cover-finite-free-local-fp-flat], and hence the map is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion]. It is finite locally free by [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. For each prime of $C$, choose in an algebraic closure of its residue field roots of the nonzero $u_i$; these are nonzero and give a point above the prime. Thus $[d]_T$ is surjective, including when the characteristic divides $d$. For $r=0$ the algebra is $C$.

source.place: Tag 04GG, lemma-characterize-henselian (monic quotient calculation); Tag 00NX, lemma-finite-projective (finite free is flat); explicit Laurent-coordinate calculation.

proof.text: The proper smooth geometrically connected group $A$ is an abelian variety by [def-sc-abelian-variety]. Its multiplication $[d]_A$ is finite locally free by [lem-sc-mult-n-finite-flat] and surjective by [lem-sc-mult-n-isogeny]. The three multiplication maps give a compatible diagram from the given exact sequence $0\to T\to H\to A\to0$ to itself: every group homomorphism commutes with a sum of $d$ copies. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-flat-homomorphism-extensions] to this diagram, using step 1 on the kernels. It follows that $[d]_H$ is finite locally free and surjective. In particular it is flat, locally finitely presented and has finite fibres. This conclusion holds for every geometric fibre of $p$.

source.place: Tag 0BFG, lemma-degree-multiplication-by-d; Tag 03RP, proposition-review-abelian-varieties; extension assembly using descent Tag 02VO.

proof.text: The map $m=[d]:G\to G$ is locally of finite presentation by [lem-a1-map-over-base-finite-presentation], with both structure maps equal to the finitely presented $p$. In fact it is of finite presentation. To check this, restrict the base to any affine open $V\subset S$. The scheme $G_V$ is quasi-compact since $p$ is quasi-compact, and quasi-separated since it is separated over the affine scheme $V$ ([lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](2)). Thus the endomorphism $m_V:G_V\to G_V$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1). These properties hold for $m$ by locality on its target: the opens $G_V$ cover the target and $m^{-1}(G_V)=G_V$. For quasi-compactness use [lem-pc-quasi-compact-local-on-target]; quasi-separatedness follows by applying the same assertion to its diagonal. Consequently $m$ is locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated, which is finite presentation by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation].

source.place: Tag 02FV, lemma-finite-presentation-permanence; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03KG, lemma-quasi-compact-local, clause (6), specialized to schemes.

proof.text: For $s\in S$ choose an algebraic closure $k$ of $\kappa(s)$. The map $\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is an fpqc covering by [lem-pc-field-extension-fpqc-cover]. Its base change to the target $G_s$ is flat and surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. At any point of $G_s$ choose a point above it; step 2 says that the geometric base change of $m_s$ is flat at every point. Thus [lem-sfb-pointwise-flatness-base-change](2) shows that $m_s$ is flat everywhere. Now $p$ is flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-pc-smooth-flat], and its target copy is locally of finite type. Apply [lem-sfb-fibrewise-flatness-criterion] at each point of the source $G$ to conclude that $m$ is flat.

source.place: Tag 039C, theorem-criterion-flatness-fibre, structure sheaf; morphisms.tex flat base change and pointwise descent.

proof.text: Surjectivity of $m$ follows from step 2: given a point $y$ of its target, put $s=p(y)$, lift $y$ to the geometric base change $G_k$ using [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] and [lem-pc-field-extension-fpqc-cover], and then lift this point along the surjective $[d]_{G_k}$. Projecting back gives a preimage of $y$. Also $m$ is quasi-finite at every point. Indeed every point $x$ of $G_s$ lifts under the same surjective geometric base change; the upstairs map is finite by step 2 and hence quasi-finite by [pqf-lem-finite-qf], and [lem-sfb-scheme-quasifinite-at-base-change] descends quasi-finiteness at this point first to $m_s$ and then to $m$. The latter application uses the arbitrary base change $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$ on the two copies of $G$, viewed as the corresponding base change on the target. Together with quasi-compactness from step 3, [pqf-lem-qf-locqf-qc] gives quasi-finiteness. Its fibres are finite: after an algebraically closed extension of the residue field of a target point, the fibre is a fibre of the finite map from step 2, so is finite; the surjective projection back to the original fibre shows that it too has finitely many points. This is the finite-fibre conclusion of the item, as in [pqf-def-quasifinite].

source.place: Tag 01TM, lemma-base-change-quasi-finite, clause (1); surjectivity checked by geometric lifting.

proof.text: Flatness, surjectivity and finite presentation give an fppf covering by [def-pc-fppf-site]. Quasi-compactness is part of finite presentation, so it is also an fpqc covering by [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]: over an affine target open its quasi-compact inverse image has a finite affine cover, whose images cover the target open. This proves the asserted covering properties with no condition on $d$ beyond positivity.

source.place: Tags 021L and 022B, covering definitions; finite affine refinement for a quasi-compact inverse image.

proof.text: Write $R_1=G$ with its structure map $p$, and for $a\geq1$ use the common value map $R_a\to G$ to identify $R_{a+1}=R_a\times_{G,m}G$. Its projection to $R_a$ is a base change of $m$, so is flat and of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). Inductively $R_a\to S$ is flat by [lem-pc-flat-compose]. It is of finite presentation as well: local finite presentation composes by [lem-sbc-locally-finite-presentation-composition]; on every affine open $V\subset S$, the successive inverse images are quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](2), starting from $G_V$. Thus the composites are quasi-compact and quasi-separated locally on $S$, and [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] applies. For local Noetherianity choose a Noetherian affine neighbourhood $V$ of each point of $S$. The scheme $(R_a)_V$ is of finite type over $V$, hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. These opens cover $R_a$.

source.place: Tags 01TR (lemma-composition-finite-presentation), 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), flat base change and composition.

proof.text: For an open $U\subseteq S$, a test scheme over $U$ maps to $R_a\times_SU$ exactly when it gives $a$ maps to $G_U$ whose images under the restricted $m_U$ agree. The fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] therefore identifies $R_a\times_SU$ with the stated iterated relation scheme over $U$, compatibly with its projections. The formulas are unchanged for $a=1$.

source.place: Fibre-product universal property, applied to open restriction.
